name: engine_start

description: Start real-time playback on the audio device (jack) or without one (dummy). backend: jack (default; PipeWire's JACK or a JACK server) or dummy (no device, paced like one). block: the device block in frames (default 256); the device's period may differ and is reported. anticipative (default true): render ahead of the playhead on worker threads (edits are heard up to 200 ms later); false renders everything in the audio callback. The engine runs at the device's rate (media is resampled; renders stay at the project's rate). See describe for errors and examples.

name: engine_status
title: Real-time engine state: backend, rate, block, device period, latency, xruns.
description: Real-time engine state: backend, rate, block, device period, latency, xruns. plan_latency: the session's plugin delay in frames; device_latency: frames from the engine's outputs to the device. restart_needed: the device changed rate or went away; engine.stop and engine.start again. failed_fx: isolated plugins whose process crashed or hung (silent now; fx.restart re-creates them). See describe for errors and examples.

name: engine_stop

description: Stop real-time playback and release the audio device.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: env_add

Target one of track (param volume|trim|pan|width|mute), route (volume|pan|mute) or fx (a semantic key such as "gain" or "filter1.cutoff", or for other plugins a CLAP id or parameter name). points: [{beat|bar|seconds, value, shape?, tension?}]; values in the parameter's unit (dB, %, Hz… — text like "800 Hz" works for plugins); shapes linear, square, slow, fast_start, fast_end, bezier. Plugin values move along the parameter's curve (a log cutoff sweeps evenly in pitch). See describe for errors and examples.

name: midi_edit
title: Edit a MIDI item's notes and CCs: add, remove, move, resize, velocity, quantize.
description: Edit a MIDI item's notes and CCs: add, remove, move, resize, velocity, quantize. ops run in order and are one undo step. notes: indices into midi.notes' list as it was before this command (every op refers to that list, so later ops are not affected by earlier removals). Beats are from the item's start. add {pitch, start, length, velocity?, channel?}; remove {notes}; move {notes, beats?, semitones?}; resize {notes, length? | length_delta? | start_delta?}; velocity {notes, velocity? and/or velocity_delta?}; quantize {notes? (all), grid (beats, on the project's grid), strength? 0-1, ends?}; cc.set {number, points [{beat, value}], channel?}; cc.clear {number, from?, to?}. Returns the new indices of the notes the ops added or changed (to keep a selection). See describe for errors and examples.

name: route_add
title: Send one track to another track, bus, the master, or a plug-in's key.
description: Send one track to another track, bus, the master, or a plug-in's key. The destination must not feed the source. Master accepts routes. With fx instead of to, the send feeds that plug-in's sidechain (key) input — e.g. a kick keying a compressor on the bass; it is delay-compensated, and soloing the keyed track does not stop the key. Hardware routing is not supported yet. See describe for errors and examples.

fx.description: Feed this plug-in's sidechain (key) input instead of a track's input; `to` may be left out

A pair is blocked when the source's rule applies (masters feed only keys), the destination's rule applies (channels take only hardware audio), it is the same strip, or it is listed in cycles (the destination already feeds the source). sends: existing routes per pair. Otherwise route.add accepts the pair. See describe for errors and examples.
